Rashi on Yevamot 22b:10:1.english: And she is the daughter of his father’s wife - [Meaning] that she was born to his father through marriage, and not through rape.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:11:1.hebrew: מכדי כתיב ערות אחותך בת אביך - ובין מן האונסין ובין מן הנשואין משמע. "ערות בת אשת אביך מולדת אביך" למה לי? הא נמי אחותו בת אביו היא! שמעת מינה לחייבו משום שני לאוין הללו, ואם שוגג, חייב שתי חטאות:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:11:1.english: Since it is written: “The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father” - And [this] implies both [a sister born] from rape and [one born] from marriage. Why do I [need], “The nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, begotten of your father”? She too is his sister, his father’s daughter! From this you learn [that it comes] to make him liable for these two negative commandments, and if [he transgressed] unwittingly, he is liable [to bring] two sin-offerings.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:11:2.english: She is your sister - [It] is written in this verse of "the daughter of your father's wife."

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:13:1.hebrew: לחייבו על אחותו - מן האונסין, בת אביו ובת אמו, כגון נולדו הוא והיא מן אנוסה. דמההוא קרא דאונסין לא שמעי' אלא בת אביו שלא בת אמו, דכתי' ״בת אביך או בת אמך״. והא דכתיב נמי ״בת אשת אביך״, דמשמע בין אמו בין שאין אמו, באישות הוא דכתיב, אבל באונסין לא שמעינן. להכי כתיב ״אחותו״, לרבות בת אביו ובת אמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:13:1.english: To hold him liable for [having relations with] his sister - [This refers to a sister born] out of rape, [who is] the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother — for example, [where] he and she were born from a woman who was raped. For from that verse regarding rape we derive only [the case of] the daughter of his father who is not the daughter of his mother, as it is written: "the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother." And that which is also written, "the daughter of your father's wife," which implies both [a sister who is the daughter of] his mother and [one who is] not [the daughter of] his mother, is written regarding marriage, but regarding rape we do not derive [it from there]. Therefore "his sister" is written, to include the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:13:2.hebrew: מן הדין - מק"ו: אם על בת אביו שלא בת אמו הזהיר, על בת אביו ואמו לכ"ש:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:13:2.english: From logical derivation - From an a fortiori inference: if He prohibited [relations with] his father's daughter who is not his mother's daughter, [then relations with] his father's and mother's [daughter] all the more so.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:15:1.hebrew: שלא תאמר בעלמא מזהירין מן הדין - והוי לאו גמור. ומהכא לא ילפינן למימר מדאיצטריך אחותך, אלמא אין מזהירין מן הדין — דאיכא לשנויי: מילתא דאתיא בק"ו טרח וכתב לה קרא. להכי כתב היא, כלומר: הכא הוא דאייתר קרא, אבל אזהרת דין ק"ו לאו אזהרה היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:15:1.english: So that you not say that generally we derive prohibitions by way of a logical derivation - and it would be a full-fledged negative commandment. And from here [alone] we would not learn [this] — to say, "Since 'your sister' was necessary, evidently we do not derive prohibitions from a logical derivation" — because one could answer: something that can be derived through an a fortiori inference, Scripture took the trouble to write explicitly. Therefore it wrote "she is," meaning to say: here the verse is superfluous, whereas a prohibition [derived by] an a fortiori inference is not a [valid] prohibition.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:17:1.hebrew: באידך קרא - גבי אחותך בת אביך דלא הוזכר שם אישות, דנפקי אונסין מיניה, דבנשואין אשמעינן אף בבת אביו ובבת אמו. מדכתיבא הכא, ש"מ למימרא דאע"ג דהיא בת אשת אביו, לא מחייב אלא משום אחותו:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:17:1.english: In the other verse - With regard to [the verse], "your sister, the daughter of your father," where marriage is not mentioned, from which [a sister born through] rape is derived, for in [a case of] marriage it teaches us [the prohibition] even regarding the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother. Since it ["she is your sister"] is written here [in the verse of "the daughter of your father's wife"], learn from this [that it comes] to say that even though she is the daughter of his father's wife, he is only liable on account of [her being] his sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:18:1.hebrew: שאין אישות לאביך בה - בשפחה ועובדת כוכבים, לא תפסי בה קדושין. במסכת קדושין נפקא לן מקראי בפ' האומר לחברו בסופו (דף סח.): שפחה — עם הדומה לחמור; ועובדת כוכבים — כדכתיב: ״ואחר כן תבא עליה ובעלתה״ (דברים כ״א:י״ג), ומעיקרא לא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:18:1.english: With whom your father has no marital ties - With a maidservant or an idolatress, betrothal does not take effect with her. In tractate Kiddushin, we derive [this] from verses at the end of the chapter [entitled] HaOmer LeChavero (68a): [regarding] a maidservant — [she is included in] “a people akin to a donkey”; and [regarding] an idolatress — as it is written: “and after that you may go in unto her and be her husband” (Deuteronomy 21:13), [implying that] beforehand, [betrothal does] not [take effect].

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:19:1.english: And say: To exclude his sister from his [father's] rape victim - For your father had no marital bond with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:1:1.hebrew: מיזקק נמי זקיק - לאשת אחיו ליבום, שאפילו אין כאן אח אלא ממזר זה, זקוקה לחליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:1:1.english: He also binds - his brother's wife for levirate marriage, for even if there is no brother here other than this mamzer, she is bound for chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:21:1.hebrew: כאן באונסין - ערות בת בנך מאנוסתו לא תגלה, הא בת בנה מאיש אחר גלה, דלאו אשתך היא. ומיהו בנו מן האונסין בנו הוא, וכן בתו; הלכך, גבי אחוה נמי אחוה הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:21:1.english: Here, [it is] in [a case of] rape - "The nakedness of your son's daughter" from a woman he raped, "you shall not uncover" — [implying that] her son's daughter from another man you may uncover, for she is not your wife. However, his son from rape is his son, and likewise his daughter [is his daughter]; therefore, regarding brotherhood as well, it is [considered] brotherhood.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:2:1.hebrew: וליטמא לו - אם כהן הוא ולו אח ממזר, מיטמא לו:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:2:1.english: And to become ritually impure for him - If he is a priest and he has a mamzer brother, he becomes ritually impure for him.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:3:1.english: Except for his kin - This is his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:4:1.english: She stands to be sent out [i.e., divorced] - Therefore, she is not his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:5:1.hebrew: עובדת כוכבים - לקמן מפרש בשמעתין מ"כי יסיר את בנך מאחרי":
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:5:1.english: An idolatress - Further on in our sugya, [the Gemara] explains [the source for this] from [the verse], "For he will turn away your son from following Me."

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:5:2.english: The wife and her children - [This] is written regarding a maidservant.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:6:1.hebrew: ובן אין לו - מצי למכתב ובן אן לו, כדאמרינן בקדושין (דף ד.) אן כסף, וכמו מאן יבמי (דברים כ״ה:ז׳), מאן בלעם (במדבר כ״ב:י״ד). ולהכי כתב אין, למידרש עיין עליו, דאם יש לו בן בעולם, פוטר:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:6:1.english: And he has no [ein lo] son - [The verse] could have written uven an lo [without a yod], as we say in Kiddushin (4a) [regarding] an kesef, and like me'en yevami ("my brother-in-law has refused," Deuteronomy 25:7) [and] me'en Bil'am ("Balaam has refused," Numbers 22:14). Therefore, it wrote ein [with a yod] in order to expound [it as] ayyen alav ("investigate him"), [teaching] that if he has any son in the world, he exempts [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:7:1.hebrew: בעושה מעשה עמך - והאי אביו לאו עושה מעשה עמך הוא, שהרי בא על הערוה והוליד ממנה ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:7:1.english: To one who acts according to the deeds of your people - And this father of his is not one who acts according to the deeds of your people, for behold, he had relations with a forbidden woman and fathered a mamzer from her.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:8:1.hebrew: כדאמר רב פנחס - בפ' חומר בקדש:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:8:1.english: As Rav Pinchas said - In the chapter [entitled] Chomer Bakodesh.

Rashi on Yevamot 22b:9:1.hebrew: השתא מיהת - הואיל ושב, עושה מעשה עמך הוא. ונהי נמי דעונו גלוי ונזכר כל זמן שממזר קיים, מיהו מתשובה ואילך בכלל עושה מעשה עמך הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 22b:9:1.english: At least now - Since he repented, he is [one who] "acts according to the deeds of your people." And even though his sin is exposed and remembered as long as the mamzer is alive, nevertheless from [his] repentance onward he is included among [those who] "act according to the deeds of your people."

Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:6:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא - הכא לא פריך "פשיטא, דבנו הוא", כדפריך לעיל "פשיטא, אחיו הוא", אלא אדרבה בעי "מאי טעמא". והיינו משום דשני לעיל: "נילף אחוה אחוה מבני יעקב כו'". ולהכי בעי: מאי טעמא לא ילפינן מבני יעקב דלא זקוקה, ואם כן מיפטר נמי לא ליפטר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:6:1.english: What is the reason - Here, [the Gemara] does not ask: "[Isn't it] obvious, since he is his son?" as it asks above: "[Isn't it] obvious, [as] he is his brother?" Rather, on the contrary, it asks: "What is the reason?" And this is because [the Gemara] answered above: "Let us derive [via a verbal analogy of] 'brotherhood' [and] 'brotherhood' from the sons of Jacob, etc." And therefore it asks: What is the reason we do not derive from the sons of Jacob that she is not bound [to a mamzer in levirate marriage], and if so, [a mamzer son] should not exempt [her] either.

Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:6:2.hebrew: בן אין לו עיין עליו - אע"ג דסתם אח ובן הוי אפילו ממזר, כדפריך לעיל: "פשיטא, אחיו הוא!" והכא נמי לא איצטריך "ובן אין לו — עיין עליו" אלא משום דלא נילף מבני יעקב. [והא דאיצטריך "וזרע אין לה — עיין עלה", היינו משום] דסתם זרע לא הוי אלא זרע כשר, כדאמר בריש קדושין (דף ד.): "אין לי אלא זרע כשר, זרע פסול מנין?" ולענין בני בנים הוי איפכא; דזרע משמע אפי' בני בנים, כדמשמע נמי התם דקאמר: "זרע זרעה לא צריך קרא, דבני בנים הרי הן כבנים". ובן לא משמע אלא בן לבדו, כדאמר ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קטו. ושם): "אין לי אלא בן, ובן הבן ובת הבן — בן בת הבן מנין?" ונראה לר"י דמ"עיין עליו" דהכא גבי יבום, אין לדרוש בן הבת ובת הבן [שיפטור מן היבום, כיון דאפקינן לאתויי ממזר. ולהכי איצטריך לאתויי בן הבן ובת הבן לענין נחלה, ולא בעי למילף מדלענין יבום בן ובן הבן כי הדדי נינהו, לענין נחלה נמי כי הדדי נינהו, כדאמר התם (שם דף קט. ושם) גבי בת. וא"ת: ונדרוש איפכא — גבי נחלה לאתויי ממזר, ומ"אין לו" דגבי יבום נדרוש בן הבן? וי"ל, דגבי נחלה א"צ לאתויי ממזר, דלכל מילי בנו הוא, אלא דלענין יבום הוה ס"ד למילף מבני יעקב; ולהכי ע"כ ההוא דנחלה אתא לרבות בן הבן. והא דפשיט ליה ביש נוחלין דלענין יבום בן ובת כי הדדי נינהו — נראה לר"י דנפקא לן מ"לא ימחה" — פרט לזה שאין שמו מחוי; א"נ, דבת וממזר שקולים, ובת נמי נפקא מ"עיין עליו" דהכא. ומיהו קשה לר"י: דהיכי נוכל לומר דשקולים הם בת וממזר? הא כיון דמצינו לאוקומי "עיין עליו" בבת, מהיכי תיתי לאוקומי אף בממזר, כיון דמ"אחוה אחוה" משמע למעוטי ממזר? וי"ל: כיון ד"אחוה אחוה" איצטריך לדרשא אחריתי, לית לן למעוטי מיניה ממזר לענין יבום, כיון דלכל מילי חשיב בן ואח, ולגבי יבום נמי מצי לרבויי בהדיא בת מ"עיין עליו"; הלכך, אע"ג דאיצטריך לרבויי בת, לא נניח בשביל כך מלרבויי ממזר. תדע, דהא ריש לקיש דריש לה בריש החולץ (לקמן יבמות לה: ושם) למילתא אחריתי, ואפ"ה מרבינן מיניה ממזר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:6:2.english: "He has no child" — investigate him [ayyen alav]: Even though an unspecified "brother" or "son" includes even a mamzer — as [the Gemara] asks earlier: "It is obvious, he is his brother!" — and here too, "And he has no child — investigate him" is only needed so that we do not derive [the law] from the sons of Jacob. And the reason that "and she has no seed — investigate her" is needed is because an unspecified "seed" refers only to fit seed, as [the Gemara] states at the beginning of Kiddushin (4a): "I have only fit seed; from where [do I include] disqualified seed?" But with respect to grandchildren it is the opposite: "seed" implies even grandchildren, as is also implied there, where [the Gemara] says: "Her seed's seed does not require a verse, for grandchildren are like children." Whereas "son" implies only a son himself, as [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 115a and there): "I have only a son, and a son's son, and a son's daughter; from where [do I include] a son's daughter's son?" And it appears to the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that from "investigate him" here regarding levirate marriage, one should not expound a daughter's son or a son's daughter as exempting from levirate marriage, since we have already used it to include a mamzer. Therefore, a verse is needed to include a son's son and a son's daughter with respect to inheritance, and [the Gemara] could not derive that just as for levirate marriage a son and a son's son are equal, so too for inheritance they are equal, as it says there (ibid. 109a and there) regarding a daughter. And if you ask: Let us expound the opposite — with respect to inheritance, to include a mamzer, and from "he has no [child]" regarding levirate marriage, let us expound a son's son? One can answer that with respect to inheritance there is no need to include a mamzer, for in all respects he is his son; rather, with respect to levirate marriage one might have thought to derive [the law] from the sons of Jacob. Therefore, perforce, that [verse] of inheritance comes to include a son's son. And as for what is obvious to [the Gemara] in Yesh Nochalin that with respect to levirate marriage a son and a daughter are equal — it appears to the Ri that we derive it from "shall not be blotted out" (Deuteronomy 25:6), excluding this [man] whose name is not blotted out [because he has a daughter]. Alternatively, a daughter and a mamzer are equivalent, and a daughter is also derived from "investigate him" here. However, the Ri finds this difficult: how can we say that a daughter and a mamzer are equivalent? Since we can establish "investigate him" as referring to a daughter, on what basis would we establish it as referring also to a mamzer, given that from the verbal analogy of "brotherhood, brotherhood" [achavah achavah] it is implied to exclude a mamzer? One can answer: since "brotherhood, brotherhood" is needed for another exposition, we should not exclude a mamzer from it with respect to levirate marriage, since in all respects he is considered a son and a brother, and with respect to levirate marriage as well one can explicitly include a daughter from "investigate him." Therefore, even though it is needed to include a daughter, we will not refrain on that account from including a mamzer. Know [that this is so], for Reish Lakish expounds it at the beginning of [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 35b and there) for another matter, and even so we include a mamzer from it.

Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:8:1.hebrew: כשעשה תשובה - והא דאמר בפ' הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פה: ושם): "לכל אין הבן נעשה שליח לאביו להכותו ולקללו, חוץ ממסית כו'" — התם כשעשה תשובה. וא"ת: בשלמא מלקות משכחת דמחייב אע"פ שעשה תשובה, אלא לקללו — מי שעשה תשובה אין רשאי לקללו אפילו אחר. ויש לומר, דאם הזכיר שם שמים לבטלה או עשה דבר שנתחייב בו נדוי, אף על פי שעשה תשובה — חייב ולא מיפטר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 22b:8:1.english: When he performed repentance - And that which [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] HaNekhanakin (Sanhedrin 85b and there): "For all [offenses] a son cannot be made an agent [of the court] against his father to strike him or to curse him, except for an instigator [to idolatry], etc." — there [too, it is referring to] when he performed repentance. And if you will say: Granted, [regarding] lashes, you find that he is liable [to be lashed] even though he performed repentance; however, [regarding] cursing him — one who performed repentance, even another person is not permitted to curse him! And one can say that if he mentioned the Name of Heaven in vain or did something for which he became liable to excommunication, even though he performed repentance, he is liable and is not exempted.
